newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy renews support for Slovenia, Romania in NATO.
newsitem.headline: Italy renews support for Slovenia, Romania in NATO.

text.p: Italy renewed its support on Friday for bids by Romania and Slovenia to join NATO, and said that decisions on expanding the western alliance would require unanimous consent from existing members.
"Italy certainly favours the entry of Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary," Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said in a speech on Italy's relations with central and eastern Europe.
"But with these, it believes that at least two other countries must be included in the first wave of new members," Dini said, citing neighbour Slovenia and Romania.
The United States told a NATO meeting in Brussels on Thursday that only Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic should be in NATO's first wave of expansion.
Although Washington's view is expected to be decisive, some European allies have already vowed to fight on, at the alliance's July 8-9 summit in Madrid, for Slovenia and Romania to be invited in.
"In NATO, decisions have to be taken by unanimity," Dini told journalists before his speech.
"We have had an initial exchange of ideas, we knew that this was the position of the United States, but a definitive decision shall be taken in Madrid," Dini added.
In his speech, Dini defended Slovenia's admission, saying the small Balkan nation plays a "crucial strategic-military role in connecting Hungary to other members of the alliance".
Dini said that Slovenia had also played an important part in international mediation after the break-up of Yugoslavia.
Romania, which borders the Black Sea, "would provide a needed equilibrium in the south of the alliance", Dini added.
France and other European nations also support granting NATO admission to Romania and Slovenia.
